claim: llm-d v0.8 introduced the FileDiscovery plugin, enabling the routing layer to discover inference endpoints through filesystem-based service discovery rather than the Kubernetes API, unlocking deployment on Slurm clusters and bare-metal research labs.
stance_target: llm-d router already has a documented non-Kubernetes discovery mechanism as of a specific release
scope_conditions: llm-d v0.8 release, dated ~mid-2026 (v0.9 milestone described as targeting 'early August')
quoted_support: The FileDiscovery plugin enables llm-d's routing layer to discover inference endpoints through filesystem-based service discovery rather than the Kubernetes API. Operators write endpoint addresses to a file; the router watches it.

claim: Component renames at v0.8: llm-d-inference-scheduler became llm-d-router-endpoint-picker, and llm-d-routing-sidecar became llm-d-router-disagg-sidecar, reflecting that both are components of the llm-d Router rather than standalone systems.
stance_target: naming/identity of the components a fork/customization effort would need to target
quoted_support: The component renames in this release reflect the same thinking. `llm-d-inference-scheduler` becomes `llm-d-router-endpoint-picker`. `llm-d-routing-sidecar` becomes `llm-d-router-disagg-sidecar`.

claim: As of v0.8, llm-d dropped custom-built vLLM images for most platforms, defaulting to unmodified upstream vllm/vllm-openai:v0.23.0 (GPU), vllm/vllm-openai-rocm (AMD), and prebuilt upstream vLLM XPU image (Intel), removing llm-d-cuda-gb200, llm-d-xpu, and llm-d-rocm images; llm-d-cuda remains for custom wheel builds (DeepGEMM, DeepEP). Intel Gaudi (HPU) support was removed entirely because upstream vLLM does not maintain Gaudi images.
stance_target: llm-d's positioning as a control plane atop unmodified inference engines rather than a forked distribution
quoted_support: The default GPU image is now `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.23.0` - the upstream release, unmodified... This is not just a packaging simplification - it is a statement about what llm-d is. The project is a control plane that wraps inference engines, not a distribution that replaces them.

claim: SGLang became a first-class second inference backend alongside vLLM at v0.8, supported across optimized-baseline, precise-prefix-cache-routing, tiered-prefix-cache, and P/D disaggregation well-lit paths (wide expert parallelism not yet covered); TensorRT-LLM was added as a third backend via trtllm-serve with a full recipe and optimized-baseline guide.
stance_target: llm-d's routing/scoring layer (prefix-cache scorer specifically) already generalizes across multiple inference engine backends, evidence that the architecture separates routing logic from backend specifics
quoted_support: SGLang joins vLLM as a supported inference backend across the optimized baseline, precise prefix cache routing, tiered prefix cache, and P/D disaggregation well-lit paths... The prefix cache scorer, previously vLLM-only, now works with SGLang backends with optimal configuration and benchmark numbers.

claim: At v0.8, llm-d's infrastructure dependencies pinned Gateway API Inference Extension (GAIE) to v1.5.0, with GAIE Helm charts published from the llm-d-router OCI registry; the Workload Variant Autoscaler (WVA) CRD migrated to the llm-d.ai API group as a breaking change.
stance_target: exact dependency/API versions to target when building against this era of llm-d
quoted_support: Infrastructure dependencies update to Istio 1.29.4, kgateway/agentgateway v2.3.3, and Gateway API Inference Extension v1.5.0, with the GAIE Helm charts now published from the llm-d-router OCI registry.
